findings.evidenceJa: 電灯の消えたフロアを
findings.governingReading: Shinji flees through an unlit floor.
findings.explanation: Though is a conspicuous typo for through and momentarily breaks the movement.

findings.governingReading: The narration presents Matou Shinji’s full name continuously.
findings.explanation: The Japanese witness breaks the visual line within the name, but mirror moon’s corresponding presentation also leaves the sentence awkwardly broken after a hyphen; the rendered name/action unit is disrupted.

findings.highlight: the fact the he isn’t a Master any more
findings.evidenceJa: マスターでなくなった事より
findings.governingReading: More than losing his status as Master, Shinji prioritizes his life.
findings.explanation: The missing t in that produces a basic grammatical corruption in a key priority statement.

findings.governingReading: Shinji had ordered Rider not to kill Saber too easily, so that he could torment and corner her.
findings.explanation: Quickly shifts the prohibition from an easy immediate kill to speed and pluralizes the victim, weakening Shinji’s responsibility for prolonging the fight.

findings.governingReading: An impossible sound follows when Shinji punches what he mistakes for a wall.
findings.explanation: Unlikely weakens the certainty and horror of the bodily break.

findings.evidenceJa: 楽しげな笑い声がこぼれる
findings.governingReading: Illya’s delighted laughter spills into the taut darkness.
findings.explanation: The English removes the pleasure that fuses her childlike manner with lethal cruelty.

findings.governingReading: The instant Shinji recognizes what stands before him, he is annihilated or erased.
findings.explanation: Terminated sounds administrative or computational and blunts the supernatural finality of his disappearance.

findings.evidenceJa: なにしろ他に雑音がない
findings.governingReading: Following Shinji is easy because no other noise competes with his echoing footsteps.
findings.explanation: The standalone because-clause is grammatically incomplete.

findings.governingReading: Shirou’s senses freeze before his trained body reacts.
findings.explanation: Mind replaces sensory arrest and weakens the deliberate contrast between thought and trained sensation.

findings.highlight: her breathing is weak yet irregular
findings.evidenceJa: 呼吸は弱々しいクセに激しく
findings.governingReading: Saber’s breathing is weak yet violent or rapid, as if she is delirious with fever.
findings.explanation: Irregular invents rhythm and removes the paradoxical intensity of breaths too weak to sustain her.

findings.highlight: her only reply is heavy breathing
findings.governingReading: Only Saber’s suffering, labored breathing answers Shirou.
findings.explanation: Heavy describes effort but removes the explicitly painful quality of her condition.
